newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schwarz Pharma to market new drug in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Schwarz Pharma to market new drug in U.S..

text.p: German drugs group Schwarz Pharma AG on Thursday said it had entered into an agreement with Canadian group Axcan Pharma Inc to sell the group's new liver drug in the United States.
Schwarz Pharma, fresh from entering a similar marketing agreement with U.S. group Lynx Therapeutics, also said it was taking a four percent stake in Axcan Pharma.
The two groups will each hold a 50 percent stake in Axcan Schwarz, the newly established group, and estimate sales of the URSO drug can total $100 million annually.

Schwarz Pharma beat out competitors for rights to jointly market URSO, used to treat liver disease primary biliary cirrhosis, only days after U.S. health officials approved the drug and Axcan said it was looking for a marketing partner.
At that time the Canadian group said it was in talks with several U.S. pharmaceutical firms eager to market the new drug.
Since floating its shares on the bourse last year, Schwarz Pharma has entered a number of joint-ventures in the United States in a bid to strengthen its international sales base.

The group, receiving top marks from analysts as a promising small drugs group, has focused resources on forming marketing agreements for innovative drugs rather than concentrating resources largely on building up its own drugs pipeline.
Schwarz Pharma said Axcan will seek to receive U.S. Food and Drug Adminstration approval for the drug to be used to treat other diseases, including a form of hepatitis, as well.

Family-owned Schwarz Pharma said 1996 sales are expected to be near $800 million, matching earlier made forecasts. Last year the group had sales of 1.01 billion marks and forecast a 15 percent rise in sales this year.
